summary.en: Great-nephew and adopted heir of Julius Caesar, Octavian defeated Antony and Cleopatra at Actium and in 27 BCE received the name Augustus. His long reign turned the Republic into a monarchy and began two centuries of relative peace.
summary.zh: 屋大维是尤利乌斯·恺撒的甥孙和养子，他在亚克兴击败安东尼与克娄巴特拉，于公元前27年获“奥古斯都”称号。他漫长的统治将共和国转变为君主制，开启了约两个世纪的相对和平。

label.zh: 生于罗马

summary.en: Proclaimed emperor by the army at York in 306, Constantine won the West at the Milvian Bridge in 312 and the whole empire in 324. He legalised and favoured Christianity, convened the Council of Nicaea and founded Constantinople.
summary.zh: 君士坦丁306年在约克被军队拥立为皇帝，312年在米尔维安桥战役中夺得西部，324年统一整个帝国。他使基督教合法化并予以扶持，召开尼西亚公会议，并建立君士坦丁堡。

summary.en: Ruler of the Huns from 434 (jointly with his brother Bleda until c. 445), Attila extracted huge tributes from the Eastern Roman Empire and invaded Gaul in 451 and Italy in 452. His empire collapsed soon after his death in 453.
summary.zh: 阿提拉自434年起统治匈人（约445年前与其兄布列达共治），向东罗马帝国勒索巨额贡金，并于451年入侵高卢、452年入侵意大利。453年他死后不久，匈人帝国即告瓦解。

summary.en: Born to a peasant family in the Balkans, Justinian ruled from Constantinople from 527. His generals reconquered North Africa, Italy and southern Spain; he codified Roman law in the Corpus Juris Civilis and rebuilt Hagia Sophia.
summary.zh: 查士丁尼出身巴尔干农家，527年起在君士坦丁堡执政。他的将领收复了北非、意大利和西班牙南部；他主持编纂《民法大全》，并重建圣索菲亚大教堂。

summary.en: King of the Franks from 768 and of the Lombards from 774, Charlemagne campaigned against Saxons, Avars and the Muslims of Spain to build an empire spanning much of western Europe. Crowned emperor in Rome in 800, he sponsored the Carolingian Renaissance from his court at Aachen.
summary.zh: 查理曼768年起为法兰克国王，774年兼领伦巴第王位，他征讨萨克森人、阿瓦尔人及西班牙穆斯林，建立了横跨西欧大部的帝国。800年他在罗马加冕称帝，并以亚琛宫廷为中心推动了“加洛林文艺复兴”。

summary.en: Illegitimate son of Duke Robert I of Normandy, William secured his duchy after years of rebellion and invaded England in 1066, winning at Hastings. As king he replaced the English elite with Normans, built castles across the land and ordered the Domesday survey.
summary.zh: 威廉是诺曼底公爵罗贝尔一世的私生子，历经多年叛乱后稳固公国，1066年入侵英格兰并在黑斯廷斯获胜。为王期间，他以诺曼人取代英格兰原有精英，在各地修筑城堡，并下令编制《末日审判书》。

summary.en: Heiress to the duchy of Aquitaine, Eleanor married Louis VII of France and joined the Second Crusade. After their annulment in 1152 she married Henry of Anjou, soon Henry II of England; mother of Richard I and John, she remained a political force into her eighties.
summary.zh: 埃莉诺是阿基坦公国的女继承人，嫁给法王路易七世并随其参加第二次十字军东征。1152年婚姻被宣告无效后，她改嫁安茹的亨利（不久成为英格兰国王亨利二世）；作为理查一世和约翰王之母，她直至八十多岁仍活跃于政坛。

summary.zh: 贞德是来自栋雷米的农家少女，自称受圣徒之声召唤拯救法兰西，她说服王太子查理准许她参与1429年解救奥尔良。查理在兰斯加冕后，她在贡比涅被俘，经亲英法庭以异端罪审判，在鲁昂被处以火刑。

summary.en: A goldsmith from Mainz, Gutenberg experimented with printing in Strasbourg in the 1430s and developed movable metal type, oil-based ink and a press. His Mainz workshop produced the 42-line Bible about 1455; after losing a lawsuit to his financier Johann Fust he continued printing on a smaller scale.
summary.zh: 谷登堡是美因茨的金匠，15世纪30年代在斯特拉斯堡试验印刷，发展出金属活字、油性墨水与印刷机相结合的技术。他的美因茨作坊约于1455年印成四十二行《圣经》；在与出资人约翰·富斯特的诉讼中败诉后，他仍以较小规模继续印刷。

summary.en: A Genoese navigator who settled in Portugal, Columbus won backing from Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain for a westward route to Asia. His four voyages (1492–1504) reached the Caribbean and Central and South America, opening the Americas to European colonisation.
summary.zh: 哥伦布是热那亚航海家，曾定居葡萄牙，后获西班牙的斐迪南与伊莎贝拉资助，向西航行寻找通往亚洲的航线。他的四次航行（1492—1504年）抵达加勒比海以及中美洲和南美洲，开启了欧洲对美洲的殖民。

summary.zh: 查理五世集哈布斯堡、勃艮第和西班牙王朝遗产于一身，统治尼德兰、西班牙及其美洲帝国、意大利南部，并自1519年起为神圣罗马帝国皇帝。他与法国、奥斯曼帝国及新教诸侯连年征战，1555—1556年退位后隐居尤斯特修道院。

story.en:
Clovis inherited a small Frankish kingdom centred on Tournai around 481. In 486 he defeated Syagrius, the last Roman commander in northern Gaul, at Soissons, and over the next two decades he subdued the Alamanni, drove the Visigoths out of most of Gaul at Vouillé in 507 and eliminated rival Frankish kings, several of them his own kinsmen.

Our main source, Bishop Gregory of Tours, wrote almost a century later and shaped his account to edify. He tells of a precious vase looted from a church near Soissons: a soldier smashed it with his axe rather than let the king take it above his share. A year later, at a review of the army, Clovis split the man's skull, reminding him of the vase. Gregory also says Clovis vowed to become a Christian if the God of his wife Clotilde gave him victory over the Alamanni.

His baptism at Reims by Bishop Remigius, in a year historians still argue over, made him a Catholic rather than an Arian king and won him the backing of the Gallo-Roman bishops. Paris became his seat, and the Merovingian dynasty he founded ruled Francia for more than two centuries.
story.zh:
约481年，克洛维在图尔奈继承了一个弱小的法兰克王国。486年，他在苏瓦松击败北高卢最后一位罗马统帅西阿格里乌斯；此后二十年间，他征服阿勒曼尼人，507年在武耶击溃西哥特人、把他们逐出高卢大部，又陆续除掉其他法兰克诸王，其中好几位是他的亲族。

关于他的主要史料出自图尔主教格雷戈里之手，但成书晚了将近一个世纪，且带有劝谕色彩。据格雷戈里记载，苏瓦松附近一座教堂被劫走一只珍贵的瓶子，一名士兵宁可用斧头砸碎它，也不肯让国王在应得份额之外取走。一年后检阅军队时，克洛维以斧劈开此人头颅，并提醒他记住那只瓶子。格雷戈里还说，克洛维曾发誓：若妻子克洛蒂尔德所信的上帝助他战胜阿勒曼尼人，他便皈依基督教。

他在兰斯由主教雷米吉乌斯施洗，具体年份至今仍有争论。这使他成为信奉天主教而非阿里乌派的国王，赢得了高卢-罗马主教们的支持。他以巴黎为都，所建立的墨洛温王朝统治法兰克两百余年。

story.en:
In January 878 a Danish army under Guthrum made a surprise winter attack on the royal estate at Chippenham, and Alfred, king of Wessex since 871, was driven into the Somerset marshes at Athelney. From there he harried the Danes and called out the men of Somerset, Wiltshire and Hampshire. In May he defeated Guthrum at Edington; the Danish leader accepted baptism with Alfred as his godfather, and the two later agreed a frontier between Wessex and the Danelaw.

The best-known tale of these months, in which a herdsman's wife scolds the disguised king for letting her cakes burn, first appears in a much later life of St Neot and is almost certainly legend.

Alfred's real achievement came afterwards. He built a network of fortified burhs, reorganised the army and commissioned new ships, occupied London in 886 and issued a law code. Convinced that learning had decayed, he had key Latin works translated into English, some reputedly by his own hand, and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle was begun in his reign. His children and grandchildren used this base to unite England in the tenth century.
story.zh:
878年1月，古斯鲁姆率领的丹麦军队在隆冬突袭奇彭纳姆王室庄园，自871年起任威塞克斯国王的阿尔弗雷德被迫退入萨默塞特的阿塞尔尼沼泽。他以此为据点袭扰丹麦人，并召集萨默塞特、威尔特郡和汉普郡的民军。同年5月，他在埃丁顿击败古斯鲁姆；这位丹麦首领接受洗礼，由阿尔弗雷德担任教父，两人后来划定了威塞克斯与丹麦区之间的边界。

这几个月里最广为流传的故事，说乔装的国王因看管不力烤焦了牧人妻子的饼而遭到责骂，最早见于晚得多的《圣尼奥特传》，几乎可以肯定是传说。

阿尔弗雷德真正的功业在此之后。他修建了遍布王国的设防城镇“堡”，改组军队并督造新船，886年占领伦敦，并颁布法典。他深感学问衰微，下令把重要的拉丁著作译成英语，据说其中一些出自他本人之手；《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》也在他在位时开始编纂。他的子孙凭借这一基础，在10世纪统一了英格兰。

note: Birthplace is not recorded; Wallhausen is the usual conjecture.

story.en:
Otto was crowned king at Aachen in 936, seated on Charlemagne's throne to show whose heir he meant to be. His first twenty years were spent putting down rebellious dukes, among them his own brother Henry and later his son Liudolf. In 951 he crossed the Alps, married the widowed Italian queen Adelaide and took the Italian crown at Pavia.

The turning point came on 10 August 955 on the Lechfeld near Augsburg, where his army crushed the Magyar horsemen who had raided Germany for half a century. The Saxon monk Widukind of Corvey claims the victorious troops hailed Otto as emperor on the battlefield. The great Magyar raids into the west ceased, and the Magyars went on to settle into the kingdom of Hungary.

On 2 February 962 Pope John XII crowned Otto emperor in Rome, reviving the western imperial title in the line later known as the Holy Roman Empire. He governed through bishops and abbots as much as through nobles, founded the archbishopric of Magdeburg in 968 as a base for missions to the Slavs, and was buried in its cathedral after dying at Memleben in 973.
story.zh:
936年，奥托在亚琛加冕为王，他坐上查理曼的宝座，表明自己以查理曼的继承者自居。此后二十年，他不断镇压叛乱的公爵，其中包括他的弟弟亨利，后来还有他的儿子柳多尔夫。951年，他翻越阿尔卑斯山，迎娶守寡的意大利王后阿德尔海德，并在帕维亚取得意大利王位。

转折点出现在955年8月10日。在奥格斯堡附近的莱希费尔德，他的军队大败劫掠德意志达半个世纪之久的马扎尔骑兵。据萨克森修士科尔维的维杜金德记载，得胜的将士当场在战场上拥戴奥托为皇帝。此后马扎尔人对西欧的大规模劫掠停止了，他们逐渐定居下来，建立了匈牙利王国。

962年2月2日，教皇约翰十二世在罗马为奥托加冕，西方的皇帝称号由此复兴，这一帝统后来被称为神圣罗马帝国。他既倚重贵族，也大量任用主教和修道院长治理国家；968年设立马格德堡大主教区，作为向斯拉夫人传教的基地。973年他在梅姆勒本去世，葬于马格德堡大教堂。

note: Born c. 1122 (some say 1123); birthplace unknown. The drowning site on the Saleph (Göksu) near Silifke is approximate.

story.en:
Frederick of Hohenstaufen, whom the Italians called Barbarossa for his red beard, was elected king at Frankfurt in 1152 and crowned emperor in Rome in 1155. He set out to restore imperial rights in northern Italy, where wealthy cities such as Milan had grown used to governing themselves. At Roncaglia in 1158 his jurists listed the revenues and powers owed to the emperor; when Milan resisted he besieged it, and in 1162 had the city emptied and largely pulled down.

The cities answered by forming the Lombard League, allied with Pope Alexander III, whom Frederick had refused to recognise. At Legnano in 1176 the League's foot soldiers, rallied around their carroccio war-wagon, routed his knights. At Venice the next year Frederick knelt before Alexander, and the Peace of Constance in 1183 left the cities their self-government.

In old age he took the cross. Leading a large army overland toward the Holy Land, he drowned on 10 June 1190 while crossing the Saleph river in Cilicia. A German legend, first told of his grandson Frederick II, later held that Barbarossa sleeps inside the Kyffhäuser mountain, waiting to return.
story.zh:
霍亨施陶芬家族的腓特烈因一把红胡子被意大利人称为“巴巴罗萨”。他于1152年在法兰克福当选国王，1155年在罗马加冕为皇帝。他决心恢复帝国在意大利北部的权利，而米兰等富庶城市早已习惯自治。1158年在隆卡利亚会议上，他的法学家逐条列出应归皇帝的收入和权力；米兰拒不服从，他便兴兵围城，并于1162年下令驱散居民、把城市大半拆毁。

各城市随即结成伦巴第同盟，并与腓特烈拒不承认的教皇亚历山大三世联手。1176年在莱尼亚诺，同盟的步兵围绕着他们的战车“卡罗乔”坚守，击溃了皇帝的骑士。次年在威尼斯，腓特烈向亚历山大下跪和解；1183年的《康斯坦茨和约》则让各城保住了自治权。

晚年他誓师东征。1190年6月10日，他率大军取道陆路前往圣地，在渡过奇里乞亚的萨列夫河时溺水身亡。后来德意志流传一个传说（最初讲的是他的孙子腓特烈二世）：红胡子并没有死，而是沉睡在基夫豪塞尔山中，等待有朝一日归来。

role.en: Friar and founder of the Franciscan order

summary.en: A merchant's son from Assisi, Francis renounced his wealth to live in radical poverty and preach penance. His brotherhood, approved by Innocent III, became the Franciscan order. He preached before the sultan of Egypt in 1219 and was canonised two years after his death.
summary.zh: 方济各出身亚西西商人家庭，他放弃财产，过彻底清贫的生活并宣讲悔改。他的修士团体获教皇英诺森三世批准，发展为方济各会。1219年他曾在埃及苏丹面前布道，去世两年后被封为圣人。

label.zh: 生于亚西西

label.en: Captured in war and held prisoner at Perugia
label.zh: 战争中被俘，囚于佩鲁贾

label.en: Hears the call to rebuild San Damiano
label.zh: 在圣达米亚诺得到重修教堂的感召

label.en: Innocent III approves the brothers' way of life in Rome
label.zh: 教皇英诺森三世在罗马认可其修会会规

label.en: Preaches before Sultan al-Kamil at Damietta
label.zh: 在达米埃塔向苏丹卡米勒布道

label.en: Stages the Christmas crib at Greccio
label.zh: 在格雷乔布置圣诞马槽

label.en: Said to receive the stigmata on Mount La Verna
label.zh: 据称在拉维纳山领受圣痕

label.en: Dies at the Porziuncola below Assisi
label.zh: 卒于亚西西山下的波尔齐翁库拉

sources.title: Thomas of Celano, First Life of St Francis (1228–29)
Augustine Thompson, Francis of Assisi: A New Biography (2012)

note: Born in 1181 or 1182. The papal approval is dated 1209 or 1210.

story.en:
Francis, son of the Assisi cloth merchant Pietro di Bernardone, spent his youth in pleasure and dreams of knighthood, and was held prisoner for a year after Assisi's war with Perugia. After illness and a series of religious experiences he renounced his inheritance before the bishop of Assisi, by tradition handing back even the clothes he wore, and began repairing ruined churches such as San Damiano.

Followers gathered around him, and around 1209 Pope Innocent III gave spoken approval to their simple rule of poverty and preaching. In 1219 Francis went to the crusader camp at Damietta in Egypt and crossed the lines to preach before Sultan al-Kamil, who received him courteously and let him go; the crusader bishop Jacques de Vitry, who was in the camp, recorded the visit. At Greccio at Christmas 1223 he staged a living manger scene, and in 1224 on Mount La Verna he is said to have received the stigmata.

He died at the Porziuncola below Assisi in 1226 and was canonised two years later. The Franciscans became one of the largest orders of the medieval Church, and his Canticle of the Creatures is among the earliest poems in Italian.
story.zh:
方济各是亚西西布商彼得罗·迪·贝尔纳多内之子，青年时代纵情享乐，梦想成为骑士；在亚西西与佩鲁贾交战后，他被俘囚禁了一年。经历重病和一连串宗教体验后，他在亚西西主教面前放弃继承权，相传连身上的衣服也一并脱还给父亲，随后开始修缮圣达米亚诺等荒废的教堂。

追随者渐渐聚集到他身边。约1209年，教皇英诺森三世口头批准了他们以清贫和布道为本的简朴会规。1219年，方济各来到埃及达米埃塔城外的十字军营地，穿过两军阵线，到苏丹卡米勒面前布道；苏丹以礼相待，并放他平安返回。当时身在营中的十字军主教雅克·德·维特里记下了这次会面。1223年圣诞节，他在格雷乔布置了真人真畜的马槽场景；1224年在拉维纳山上，据说他领受了圣痕。

1226年，他在亚西西山下的波尔齐翁库拉去世，两年后即被封圣。方济各会成为中世纪教会最大的修会之一，他所作的《万物颂》也是最早的意大利语诗歌之一。

role.zh: 多明我会修士、神学家、哲学家

summary.en: A Dominican friar trained by Albert the Great, Aquinas taught in Paris, Naples and Rome and wrote the Summa theologiae, which joined Aristotelian philosophy to Christian doctrine. Canonised in 1323, he became the most influential theologian of the Catholic Church.
summary.zh: 阿奎那是多明我会修士，师从大阿尔伯特，曾在巴黎、那不勒斯和罗马执教。他撰写的《神学大全》将亚里士多德哲学与基督教教义融为一体。1323年被封为圣人，成为天主教会最具影响力的神学家。

label.en: Born at the family castle of Roccasecca
label.zh: 生于罗卡塞卡的家族城堡

label.en: Placed as an oblate at Monte Cassino
label.zh: 被送入卡西诺山修道院

label.en: Studies at the university of Naples
label.zh: 在那不勒斯大学求学

label.en: Studies under Albert the Great in Paris
label.zh: 在巴黎师从大阿尔伯特
随阿尔伯特前往科隆

label.en: Becomes master of theology at Paris
label.zh: 在巴黎成为神学教授

label.en: Teaches at Santa Sabina in Rome and begins the Summa
label.zh: 在罗马圣撒比纳修院执教并开始撰写《神学大全》
卒于福萨诺瓦修道院

sources.title: Jean-Pierre Torrell, Saint Thomas Aquinas, vol. 1: The Person and His Work (1996)
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Thomas Aquinas

note: Born c. 1225 (some say 1224 or 1226). Stop years for his studies are approximate.

story.en:
Thomas was born into a noble family at Roccasecca, between Rome and Naples, and placed as a boy at the abbey of Monte Cassino. At the university of Naples he met the new Dominican friars and joined them in 1244. His family, who had hoped he would become a Benedictine abbot, had him seized on the road and confined for about a year before letting him go.

He studied under Albert the Great in Paris and Cologne. His early biographers say that fellow students called the large, silent young man the 'dumb ox', and that Albert replied that this ox would one day bellow loud enough for the whole world to hear. Thomas went on to teach in Paris, Orvieto, Rome and Naples, writing commentaries on Aristotle, the Summa contra Gentiles and the unfinished Summa theologiae.

In December 1273, after some experience during Mass in Naples, he stopped writing, reportedly saying that everything he had written now seemed like straw. He died a few months later at the abbey of Fossanova on his way to the Council of Lyon. Canonised in 1323, he became the Church's standard theologian.
story.zh:
托马斯出身贵族，生于罗马与那不勒斯之间的罗卡塞卡，幼年被送入卡西诺山修道院。在那不勒斯大学，他结识了新兴的多明我会修士，并于1244年加入该会。家人原本希望他日后成为本笃会修道院长，于是派人在途中把他劫走，软禁了约一年才放他离去。

他先后在巴黎和科隆师从大阿尔伯特。据早期传记记载，同学们给这个身材魁梧、沉默寡言的年轻人起了个绰号叫“哑牛”，阿尔伯特却说，这头牛总有一天会发出响彻世界的吼声。此后托马斯在巴黎、奥维多、罗马和那不勒斯执教，撰写了亚里士多德著作的注释、《反异教大全》以及未完成的《神学大全》。

1273年12月，他在那不勒斯望弥撒时有过某种体验，此后便停止写作，据说他表示自己写下的一切如今看来都如同草芥。几个月后，他在前往里昂公会议的途中死于福萨诺瓦修道院。1323年他被封为圣人，其学说成为天主教会的标准神学。

summary.en: Francesco Petrarca wrote the Italian love poems to Laura that shaped the European sonnet, and searched out lost classical texts. Crowned poet laureate in Rome in 1341, he is often called the father of Renaissance humanism.
summary.zh: 弗朗切斯科·彼特拉克写下献给劳拉的意大利语情诗，塑造了欧洲十四行诗的传统，并四处搜寻失传的古典文献。他于1341年在罗马获桂冠诗人称号，常被誉为文艺复兴人文主义之父。

label.en: Born at Arezzo to an exiled Florentine family
label.zh: 生于阿雷佐的流亡佛罗伦萨家庭
在博洛尼亚学习法律

label.en: First sees Laura in Avignon, by his own account
label.zh: 据他自述，在阿维尼翁初见劳拉
记述攀登旺图山
定居沃克吕兹

label.en: Crowned poet laureate on the Capitoline
label.zh: 在卡比托利欧山获桂冠诗人称号

label.en: Moves to Milan under the Visconti
label.zh: 移居米兰，依附维斯孔蒂家族
卒于阿尔夸

sources.title: Ernest Hatch Wilkins, Life of Petrarch (1961)
Petrarch, Familiares IV.1 (the Mont Ventoux letter)

story.en:
Born at Arezzo to an exiled Florentine notary, Francesco Petrarca grew up near the papal court at Avignon and was sent to study law at Montpellier and Bologna, which he gave up for literature. On Good Friday 1327, by his own account, he first saw Laura in the church of Sainte-Claire at Avignon. His Italian poems to her, collected in the Canzoniere, set the pattern for the love sonnet across Europe for three centuries.

He also hunted for lost classical texts, finding Cicero's letters to Atticus at Verona in 1345, and wrote in Latin the works he expected to make him famous. In April 1341 he was crowned with laurel on the Capitoline Hill in Rome, deliberately reviving an ancient honour. A celebrated letter describes his ascent of Mont Ventoux in 1336, ending with him opening Augustine's Confessions at the summit; many scholars believe he composed or reworked it years later as a moral allegory.

He spent his last decades in Italy, serving the Visconti at Milan and living in Venice and Padua, and died at Arquà in 1374. Later humanists honoured him as the founder of their movement.
story.zh:
弗朗切斯科·彼特拉克的父亲是遭流放的佛罗伦萨公证人。他生于阿雷佐，在阿维尼翁教廷附近长大，曾被送往蒙彼利埃和博洛尼亚学习法律，后来弃法从文。据他自述，1327年耶稣受难日，他在阿维尼翁的圣克莱尔教堂第一次见到劳拉。他献给劳拉的意大利语诗篇后来汇编为《歌集》，此后三个世纪一直是欧洲爱情十四行诗的典范。

他还四处搜寻失传的古典文献，1345年在维罗纳发现了西塞罗致阿提库斯的书信；他用拉丁文写作，期望凭这些作品传世。1341年4月，他在罗马卡比托利欧山上被戴上桂冠，有意复兴这一古代荣誉。他有一封著名书信，记述1336年攀登旺图山，结尾写他在山顶翻开奥古斯丁的《忏悔录》；许多学者认为，这封信是他多年后撰写或改写的道德寓言。

晚年他定居意大利，曾在米兰为维斯孔蒂家族效力，也在威尼斯和帕多瓦居住，1374年卒于阿尔夸。后世人文主义者尊他为这场运动的开创者。

summary.en: Venetian-born and raised at the French court, Christine de Pizan was widowed young and became one of the first Europeans to earn a living by writing. Her Book of the City of Ladies defended women against the misogyny of learned tradition.
summary.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·德·皮桑生于威尼斯，在法国宫廷长大，年轻守寡后成为欧洲最早以写作为生的人之一。她的《女性之城》驳斥了学术传统中的厌女观念，为女性辩护。

label.zh: 生于威尼斯

label.en: Joins her father at Charles V's court in Paris
label.zh: 随父来到巴黎查理五世的宫廷

label.en: Widowed; turns to writing to support her family
label.zh: 丧夫，开始以写作养家

label.en: Writes The Book of the City of Ladies
label.zh: 撰写《女性之城》

label.en: Withdraws to the abbey at Poissy
label.zh: 隐居普瓦西修道院

label.en: Writes the Ditié de Jehanne d'Arc
label.zh: 写下《圣女贞德颂》

sources.title: Charity Cannon Willard, Christine de Pizan: Her Life and Works (1984)
Christine de Pizan, Le Livre de la Cité des Dames (1405)

note: She died c. 1430, probably at Poissy; the exact year and place are unrecorded. The year of her move to Poissy (c. 1418) is approximate.

story.en:
Christine was born in Venice and brought as a small child to Paris, where her father Tommaso da Pizzano served Charles V as astrologer and physician. She grew up on the edge of a learned court, married the royal secretary Étienne du Castel at fifteen, and was widowed at about twenty-five with three children, her mother and a niece to support and years of lawsuits over her husband's estate.

She turned to writing for a living, first poems and then prose, and found patrons among the French royal family and the dukes of Burgundy and Berry. In 1401–02 she challenged the misogyny of the Romance of the Rose in a public exchange of letters with leading scholars. In The Book of the City of Ladies (1405) she describes reading a book that runs women down, then being visited by Reason, Rectitude and Justice, who help her build an allegorical city peopled by famous women.

Around 1418, as civil war and English invasion engulfed Paris, she withdrew to the abbey at Poissy, where her daughter was a nun. Her last known work, the Ditié de Jehanne d'Arc of July 1429, celebrates Joan's victories while Joan was still alive.
story.zh:
克里斯蒂娜生于威尼斯，幼年随家人来到巴黎，她的父亲托马索·达·皮扎诺在查理五世宫中担任星相师和医生。她在一个崇尚学问的宫廷边缘长大，十五岁嫁给王室秘书艾蒂安·迪·卡斯泰尔；约二十五岁时丈夫去世，她不仅要抚养三个孩子，还要赡养母亲和一个侄女，并为丈夫的遗产打了多年官司。

她转而以写作谋生，先写诗，后写散文，赢得了法国王室以及勃艮第公爵、贝里公爵等人的赞助。1401至1402年间，她与多位知名学者公开通信论战，批评《玫瑰传奇》中的厌女观念。在《女性之城》（1405年）中，她写自己读到一本贬低女性的书，随后“理性”“正直”“公正”三位女神来访，帮助她建造一座住满杰出女性的寓言之城。

约1418年，内战和英军入侵席卷巴黎，她隐居到女儿当修女的普瓦西修道院。她已知的最后一部作品是1429年7月写成的《圣女贞德颂》，在贞德生前就歌颂了她的胜利。

role.en: Portuguese prince and sponsor of Atlantic voyages
role.zh: 葡萄牙王子、大西洋航海的赞助者

summary.en: A son of King John I of Portugal, Henry fought at Ceuta in 1415 and used the wealth of the Order of Christ to send expeditions down the West African coast and into the Atlantic. He never sailed on them himself, and his ventures opened the Portuguese slave trade.
summary.zh: 恩里克是葡萄牙国王若昂一世之子，1415年参加攻占休达之战，此后利用基督骑士团的财富派遣船队沿西非海岸南下、深入大西洋。他本人从未随船远航，他所资助的航行也开启了葡萄牙的奴隶贸易。

label.zh: 生于波尔图

label.en: Fights at the capture of Ceuta
label.zh: 参加攻占休达之战

label.en: Becomes governor of the Order of Christ, seated at Tomar
label.zh: 出任以托马尔为总部的基督骑士团总管

label.en: Leads a failed attack on Tangier
label.zh: 率军进攻丹吉尔失败
在萨格里什建立城镇

label.en: Oversees the sale of African captives at Lagos
label.zh: 在拉各斯监督分配非洲俘虏

label.en: Takes part in the capture of Alcácer Ceguer
label.zh: 参与攻占阿尔卡塞尔塞吉尔
卒于萨格里什

sources.title: Gomes Eanes de Zurara, Chronicle of the Discovery and Conquest of Guinea
Peter Russell, Prince Henry 'the Navigator': A Life (2000)

story.en:
The third surviving son of King John I of Portugal and Philippa of Lancaster, Henry first made his name at the capture of Ceuta in North Africa in 1415. As governor of the Order of Christ and lord of much of the Algarve, he used the order's revenues to send ships ever further down the African coast. In 1434 one of his squires, Gil Eanes, at last sailed past Cape Bojador, which seamen had feared as a point of no return.

Henry himself never sailed beyond Morocco. His court chronicler Gomes Eanes de Zurara praised his motives as crusade, curiosity and the hope of finding the Christian king Prester John, but gold and slaves soon drove the voyages. Zurara describes Henry on horseback at Lagos in 1444 watching the division of some 235 captive Africans, an early landmark of the Atlantic slave trade. His failed attack on Tangier in 1437 left his younger brother Fernando to die a hostage in Fez.

The famous navigation 'school' at Sagres is a later myth, though Henry did build a town there, where he died in 1460. By then Portuguese ships had passed Cape Verde and settlers had colonised Madeira and the Azores.
story.zh:
恩里克是葡萄牙国王若昂一世与兰开斯特的菲利帕所生的第三个存活的儿子，1415年在北非攻占休达一役中崭露头角。他身为基督骑士团总管和阿尔加维大片土地的领主，用骑士团的收入资助船队一次次沿非洲海岸南下。1434年，他的侍从吉尔·埃亚内斯终于驶过博哈多尔角，此前水手们一直把那里视为有去无回之地。

恩里克本人从未越过摩洛哥航行。他的宫廷史官戈梅斯·埃亚内斯·德·祖拉拉称颂他的动机是十字军精神、求知欲和寻找基督教君主祭司王约翰，但很快，黄金和奴隶成了航行的真正动力。据祖拉拉记载，1444年恩里克骑马在拉各斯，亲眼看着约235名被掳的非洲人被分配，这是大西洋奴隶贸易早期的标志性事件。1437年他进攻丹吉尔失败，致使弟弟费尔南多作为人质被扣，最终死在非斯。

所谓萨格里什“航海学校”是后世编造的神话，不过恩里克确实在那里建了一座城镇，并于1460年在那里去世。到那时，葡萄牙船只已越过佛得角，移民也已在马德拉群岛和亚速尔群岛定居。

name.zh: 卡斯蒂利亚的伊莎贝拉一世

summary.en: Isabella seized the Castilian throne in 1474 and, with her husband Ferdinand of Aragon, joined the two crowns that became Spain. Together the Catholic Monarchs set up the Spanish Inquisition, conquered Granada, expelled the Jews and sponsored Columbus in 1492.
summary.zh: 伊莎贝拉于1474年夺得卡斯蒂利亚王位，与丈夫阿拉贡的斐迪南共同统治，两国王冠由此联合成为西班牙。这对“天主教双王”设立西班牙宗教裁判所，于1492年征服格拉纳达、驱逐犹太人并资助哥伦布远航。

label.en: Born at Madrigal de las Altas Torres
label.zh: 生于马德里加尔德拉斯阿尔塔斯托雷斯

label.en: Recognised as heir at the Bulls of Guisando
label.zh: 在吉桑多石牛处被承认为王位继承人

label.en: Marries Ferdinand of Aragon secretly at Valladolid
label.zh: 在巴利亚多利德秘密嫁给阿拉贡的斐迪南
在塞哥维亚自立为女王
接受格拉纳达投降

label.en: Agrees the Capitulations of Santa Fe with Columbus
label.zh: 在圣菲与哥伦布签订协定
卒于梅迪纳德尔坎波

sources.title: Peggy K. Liss, Isabel the Queen: Life and Times (1992)
Hernando del Pulgar, Crónica de los Reyes Católicos

story.en:
Isabella was not expected to rule. She was the half-sister of King Henry IV of Castile, whose daughter Juana was widely slandered as illegitimate. In 1468, at the Bulls of Guisando, Henry recognised Isabella as his heir, and the next year she chose her own husband against his wishes. Ferdinand, heir to Aragon, crossed Castile disguised as a servant to reach her, and they were married at Valladolid in October 1469.

When Henry died in December 1474, Isabella had herself proclaimed queen in Segovia at once, without waiting for her husband, and won the war of succession against Juana's Portuguese allies. With Ferdinand, king of Aragon from 1479, she established the Spanish Inquisition, reformed the Church and royal government, and waged a ten-year war against the Nasrid emirate of Granada, which surrendered on 2 January 1492.

That year transformed Spain. In March the monarchs ordered all Jews to convert or leave their kingdoms, and in April, at the camp-city of Santa Fe, they agreed to back Columbus's westward voyage. Isabella died at Medina del Campo in 1504, leaving Castile to her daughter Juana.
story.zh:
伊莎贝拉原本不被看作王位继承人。她是卡斯蒂利亚国王恩里克四世的同父异母妹妹，而恩里克的女儿胡安娜则被广泛诋毁为私生女。1468年，恩里克在吉桑多石牛处承认伊莎贝拉为继承人；次年，她违背兄长的意愿自择夫婿。阿拉贡王位继承人斐迪南乔装成仆人穿越卡斯蒂利亚前来与她相会，两人于1469年10月在巴利亚多利德成婚。

1474年12月恩里克去世，伊莎贝拉没有等待丈夫，立即在塞哥维亚宣布自己为女王，并在随后的王位继承战争中击败了支持胡安娜的葡萄牙人。她与1479年继位为阿拉贡国王的斐迪南一起设立西班牙宗教裁判所，整顿教会和王室政府，并对纳斯尔王朝的格拉纳达埃米尔国进行了长达十年的战争，格拉纳达于1492年1月2日投降。

这一年改变了西班牙。3月，双王下令全体犹太人要么改宗、要么离境；4月，他们在圣菲营城同意资助哥伦布向西航行。1504年，伊莎贝拉在梅迪纳德尔坎波去世，把卡斯蒂利亚留给了女儿胡安娜。

role.en: Ruler of Florence and patron of the arts
role.zh: 佛罗伦萨统治者、艺术赞助人

summary.en: Called il Magnifico, Lorenzo led Florence from 1469 without holding formal office, survived the Pazzi conspiracy of 1478 and worked to keep peace among the Italian states. A poet himself, he patronised artists and scholars of Florence's Renaissance.
summary.zh: 洛伦佐人称“伟大的洛伦佐”，自1469年起不居正式官职而实际主导佛罗伦萨。他在1478年的帕齐阴谋中幸免于难，并致力于维持意大利诸国间的和平。他本人也是诗人，赞助了佛罗伦萨文艺复兴时期的众多艺术家和学者。

label.zh: 生于佛罗伦萨

label.en: Takes over the Medici leadership after his father's death
label.zh: 父亲去世后接掌美第奇家族

label.en: Wounded in the Pazzi attack in the cathedral
label.zh: 在大教堂遭帕齐家族袭击受伤

label.en: Negotiates peace in person with King Ferrante at Naples
label.zh: 亲赴那不勒斯与费兰特国王议和

label.zh: 委托修建波焦阿卡亚诺别墅

label.zh: 卒于卡雷吉别墅

sources.title: Miles J. Unger, Magnifico: The Brilliant Life and Violent Times of Lorenzo de' Medici (2008)

story.en:
Lorenzo was twenty when his father Piero died in 1469 and Florence's leading citizens asked him to take up the family's informal rule. He governed not through office but through money, patronage and allies on the key councils, while writing poetry in Tuscan himself.

On Sunday 26 April 1478, during Mass in Florence cathedral, conspirators of the Pazzi family, backed by Pope Sixtus IV and the archbishop of Pisa, attacked the Medici brothers. Giuliano was stabbed to death; Lorenzo, wounded in the neck, escaped into the sacristy. The crowd turned on the plotters, and the archbishop was hanged from a window of the Palazzo della Signoria. War with the pope and Naples followed, and in December 1479 Lorenzo sailed to Naples to bargain with King Ferrante in person, returning months later with a peace that made his reputation.

In his later years he worked to keep a balance among the Italian states and supported scholars and artists such as Poliziano, Pico della Mirandola and, according to Condivi and Vasari, the teenage Michelangelo. He died at Careggi in April 1492. Two years later a French invasion broke the balance and drove his son Piero from Florence.
story.zh:
1469年父亲皮耶罗去世时，洛伦佐年方二十，佛罗伦萨的头面人物请他接掌家族的非正式统治。他并不依靠官职，而是凭借财富、恩庇关系和在关键议会中的盟友治理城市，同时亲自用托斯卡纳方言写诗。

1478年4月26日星期日，佛罗伦萨大教堂正在举行弥撒，帕齐家族的阴谋者在教皇西克斯图斯四世和比萨大主教的支持下突然袭击美第奇兄弟。朱利亚诺被刺身亡；洛伦佐颈部受伤，逃进圣器室得以脱身。民众转而追杀密谋者，比萨大主教被吊死在领主宫的窗口。随后佛罗伦萨与教皇及那不勒斯开战。1479年12月，洛伦佐乘船前往那不勒斯，亲自与费兰特国王谈判，数月后带着和约归来，声望由此大振。

晚年，他努力维持意大利诸国之间的均势，赞助波利齐亚诺、皮科·德拉·米兰多拉等学者和艺术家；据孔迪维和瓦萨里记载，少年米开朗琪罗也曾住在他府中。1492年4月，他在卡雷吉去世。两年后法国入侵意大利，均势瓦解，他的儿子皮耶罗也被逐出佛罗伦萨。

summary.en: Michelangelo Buonarroti carved the Pietà and the David, painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling and the Last Judgment, and as chief architect of St Peter's designed its dome. Working between Florence and Rome for some seventy years, he was hailed in his own lifetime as the greatest artist alive.
summary.zh: 米开朗琪罗·博纳罗蒂雕刻了《圣殇》和《大卫》，绘制了西斯廷礼拜堂天顶画和《最后的审判》，并以圣彼得大教堂总建筑师的身份设计了其穹顶。他在佛罗伦萨和罗马之间工作约七十年，生前即被誉为当世最伟大的艺术家。

label.en: Becomes chief architect of St Peter's
label.zh: 出任圣彼得大教堂总建筑师

label.zh: 在罗马寓所去世

sources.title: Giorgio Vasari, Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors and Architects (1568 edition)
William E. Wallace, Michelangelo: The Artist, the Man and His Times (2010)

story.en:
Michelangelo Buonarroti was born at Caprese, where his father was briefly the local magistrate, and grew up in Florence. After a short apprenticeship with the painter Domenico Ghirlandaio he studied sculpture in the Medici garden near San Marco. In Rome, in his early twenties, he carved the Pietà now in St Peter's. Vasari says he cut his name across the Virgin's sash after hearing visitors credit the work to another sculptor; it is the only work he ever signed.

Back in Florence he turned a long-abandoned block of marble into the David, set up outside the Palazzo della Signoria in 1504. Pope Julius II then called him to Rome and, over his protests that he was a sculptor, set him to paint the Sistine Chapel ceiling. He worked on it from 1508 to 1512, standing on a scaffold of his own design rather than lying on his back, as legend has it.

He returned to the chapel to paint the Last Judgment (1536–41), and in 1546 became chief architect of St Peter's, whose dome was completed after his death to his design. He died in Rome aged 88; his nephew had the body carried secretly to Florence for burial in Santa Croce.
story.zh:
米开朗琪罗·博纳罗蒂生于卡普雷塞，当时他的父亲在那里短暂担任地方长官，他则在佛罗伦萨长大。他先在画家多梅尼科·吉兰达约门下短期学徒，后来在圣马可附近的美第奇花园学习雕塑。二十出头时，他在罗马雕成了如今陈列于圣彼得大教堂的《圣殇》。据瓦萨里记载，他听到参观者把这件作品归于另一位雕塑家，便在圣母胸前的衣带上刻下自己的名字；这是他唯一署名的作品。

回到佛罗伦萨后，他把一块搁置多年的大理石雕成了《大卫》，1504年立于领主宫前。随后教皇尤利乌斯二世召他到罗马，不顾他“我是雕塑家”的抗议，命他绘制西斯廷礼拜堂天顶。1508至1512年间，他站在自己设计的脚手架上作画，而非传说中那样仰卧着画。

后来他重返礼拜堂，绘制了《最后的审判》（1536—1541年）；1546年出任圣彼得大教堂总建筑师，大教堂的穹顶在他身后按照他的设计建成。他在罗马去世，享年88岁；侄子把他的遗体秘密运回佛罗伦萨，安葬在圣十字教堂。

summary.en: The leading humanist of northern Europe, Erasmus of Rotterdam wrote The Praise of Folly and published the first printed Greek New Testament in 1516. He satirised abuses in the Church and urged reform through learning, but refused to join the Protestant break with Rome.
summary.zh: 鹿特丹的伊拉斯谟是北欧最重要的人文主义者，著有《愚人颂》，并于1516年出版第一部印行的希腊文《新约》。他讽刺教会的种种弊端，主张以学问推动改革，却拒绝追随新教与罗马决裂。

离开改宗新教的巴塞尔，移居弗赖堡

sources.title: Johan Huizinga, Erasmus and the Age of Reformation (1924)
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Desiderius Erasmus

note: Birth year is disputed: Wikidata and many recent scholars give 1466, while Britannica and the Stanford Encyclopedia give 1469 (1467 is also argued). The Steyn monastery site is approximate.

story.en:
The illegitimate son of a priest, Erasmus was schooled at Deventer and, after his parents died, entered the Augustinian canons at Steyn near Gouda, where he was ordained in 1492. He escaped the cloister through service with the bishop of Cambrai and study in Paris, and spent the rest of his life moving between the Low Countries, England, Italy and Switzerland, living from patrons and the printing press.

Riding back from Italy in 1509 he conceived The Praise of Folly and, by his own account, wrote it within a week at the London house of his friend Thomas More; its Latin title, Moriae Encomium, puns on More's name. In 1516 Johann Froben at Basel printed his edition of the Greek New Testament with a fresh Latin translation, the text Luther later used for his German New Testament.

Erasmus wanted to reform the Church through learning and satire, not to split it. Catholic critics said he had laid the egg that Luther hatched; he replied that he had laid a hen's egg and Luther had hatched a quite different bird. In 1524 he attacked Luther's view of the will, and when Basel turned Protestant he moved to Freiburg. He died in Basel in 1536.
story.zh:
伊拉斯谟是一位神父的私生子，曾在代芬特尔上学，父母去世后进入豪达附近斯泰恩的奥古斯丁会修院，并于1492年领受神父圣职。后来他借为康布雷主教效力和赴巴黎求学的机会离开修院，此后一生辗转于低地国家、英格兰、意大利和瑞士之间，靠赞助人和印刷出版维持生计。

1509年，他从意大利骑马北返途中构思了《愚人颂》，据他自述，在伦敦友人托马斯·莫尔家中不到一周便写成；书的拉丁文标题“Moriae Encomium”暗含莫尔之名的双关。1516年，巴塞尔的约翰·弗罗本印行了他编订的希腊文《新约》，并附上他重新翻译的拉丁文译本，路德后来翻译德文《新约》时所依据的正是这一文本。

伊拉斯谟希望借助学问和讽刺来改革教会，而不是分裂教会。天主教的批评者说路德孵出的蛋是他下的；他回答说，自己下的是一只母鸡蛋，路德孵出来的却是完全不同的鸟。1524年，他著文批驳路德关于意志的观点；巴塞尔改宗新教后，他迁居弗赖堡。1536年，他在巴塞尔去世。

summary.en: A French lawyer turned reformer, Calvin wrote the Institutes of the Christian Religion and from 1541 made Geneva the model of a disciplined Reformed church. His theology shaped Protestant churches from Scotland and the Netherlands to Hungary and New England.
summary.zh: 加尔文原是法国的法学生，后投身宗教改革。他撰写了《基督教要义》，自1541年起把日内瓦建设成纪律严明的归正宗教会典范。他的神学深刻影响了从苏格兰、尼德兰到匈牙利和新英格兰的新教教会。

sources.title: John Calvin, preface to the Commentary on the Psalms (1557)

story.en:
Jean Calvin grew up at Noyon in Picardy, where his father worked for the cathedral chapter, and studied in Paris and then law at Orléans and Bourges. Around 1533 he embraced the evangelical cause, and after the Affair of the Placards in 1534 brought persecution in France he fled to Basel. There, in 1536, he published the first edition of the Institutes of the Christian Religion, a compact defence of Protestant teaching that he kept enlarging until 1559.

That summer, on his way to Strasbourg, he stopped for a night in Geneva. By his own later account, the preacher Guillaume Farel warned him that God would curse his quiet studies if he refused to help reform the city. Calvin stayed, was expelled with Farel in 1538, spent three years as a pastor in Strasbourg, and returned in 1541 to draft ordinances that set up pastors, elders and a Consistory to oversee morals.

His Geneva became a model for Reformed churches from Scotland to Hungary. It also burned the anti-Trinitarian Michael Servetus in 1553; Calvin backed the conviction, though he asked for a less cruel death. He founded the Geneva Academy in 1559 and died in the city in 1564.
story.zh:
让·加尔文在皮卡第的努瓦永长大，父亲为当地主教座堂的教士团办事。他先在巴黎求学，后到奥尔良和布尔日学习法律。约1533年，他倒向福音派；1534年“告示事件”后法国掀起迫害，他逃往巴塞尔，并于1536年在那里出版了《基督教要义》第一版。这部为新教教义辩护的简明著作，他此后不断增补，直到1559年。

同年夏天，他前往斯特拉斯堡途中在日内瓦借宿一夜。据他后来自述，传道人纪尧姆·法雷尔警告他：如果他拒绝协助改革这座城市，上帝必将咒诅他那安静的学术生活。加尔文于是留了下来。1538年他与法雷尔一同被逐，在斯特拉斯堡当了三年牧师，1541年重返日内瓦，起草法规，设立牧师、长老和负责监督风化的宗教法庭。

他治下的日内瓦成为从苏格兰到匈牙利各地归正宗教会的楷模。1553年，日内瓦也烧死了反三位一体论者米格尔·塞尔维特；加尔文支持定罪，但曾请求采用不那么残酷的死刑。1559年他创办日内瓦学院，1564年在日内瓦去世。

summary.en: A soldier wounded at Lepanto and a captive in Algiers for five years, Cervantes later worked as a royal commissary and tax collector before publishing Don Quixote in 1605 and 1615. The book is widely regarded as the first modern novel and the summit of Spanish literature.
summary.zh: 塞万提斯曾在勒班陀海战中负伤，又在阿尔及尔被囚五年，此后当过王室征粮官和税吏，于1605年和1615年出版《堂吉诃德》上下两部。这部作品被普遍视为第一部现代小说和西班牙文学的巅峰。

sources.title: Miguel de Cervantes, Don Quijote de la Mancha, Part I, prologue (1605)

story.en:
Miguel de Cervantes was born at Alcalá de Henares, the son of a struggling barber-surgeon. As a young man he went to Italy and joined the Spanish infantry. At Lepanto in October 1571, though ill with fever, he insisted on fighting on deck and was hit by three arquebus shots, losing the use of his left hand, a wound he remained proud of all his life.

Sailing home in 1575, he was captured by Barbary corsairs and held in Algiers for five years. He organised four escape attempts and, according to fellow captives, took the blame each time; in 1580 Trinitarian friars finally paid his ransom. Back in Spain he wrote plays and a pastoral romance, then worked as a commissary requisitioning grain for the Armada and as a tax collector, posts that landed him in prison, notably in Seville in 1597. In the prologue to Don Quixote he hints that the book was conceived in a prison.

Part I appeared in 1605 and was an immediate success; Part II followed in 1615, a few months before he died in Madrid in April 1616. Its knight and squire made it a founding work of the modern novel.
story.zh:
米格尔·德·塞万提斯生于阿尔卡拉德埃纳雷斯，父亲是个境况窘迫的理发外科医生。他年轻时前往意大利，加入西班牙步兵。1571年10月勒班陀海战时，他正发着高烧，却坚持上甲板作战，身中三颗火绳枪弹，左手从此残废；这处伤他终生引以为荣。

1575年乘船回国途中，他被北非海盗俘获，在阿尔及尔被囚五年。他先后四次组织越狱，据同囚者说，每次失败他都独自承担罪责；1580年，三位一体会修士终于为他付清赎金。回到西班牙后，他写剧本和一部田园小说，后来又为无敌舰队征购粮食、充当税吏，这些差事让他身陷囹圄，其中最著名的是1597年在塞维利亚入狱。他在《堂吉诃德》序言中暗示，这部书是在监狱里孕育的。

第一部于1605年出版，随即大获成功；第二部于1615年问世，几个月后，即1616年4月，他在马德里去世。书中的骑士与侍从使这部作品成为现代小说的奠基之作。

summary.en: From Stratford-upon-Avon, Shakespeare became the leading playwright of London's Lord Chamberlain's Men, later the King's Men, writing some 37 plays and 154 sonnets. Most of his great tragedies were written for the Globe on Bankside.
summary.zh: 莎士比亚来自埃文河畔斯特拉特福，成为伦敦宫内大臣剧团（后改称国王剧团）的首席剧作家，创作了约37部戏剧和154首十四行诗。他的大部分伟大悲剧都是为泰晤士河南岸的环球剧场而写。

sources.title: Samuel Schoenbaum, William Shakespeare: A Compact Documentary Life (1977)
Robert Greene, Greenes Groats-worth of Witte (1592)

story.en:
William Shakespeare was baptised at Stratford-upon-Avon in April 1564, the son of a glover and town official. He married Anne Hathaway in 1582 and had three children, after which the records fall silent for several years. By 1592 he was known in London: the dying writer Robert Greene sneered at an 'upstart crow' who thought himself the only 'Shake-scene' in the country.

From 1594 he acted and wrote for the Lord Chamberlain's Men, who became the King's Men under James I. When the lease on their playhouse, the Theatre in Shoreditch, ran out, the company pulled the building down in the winter of 1598–99 and carried its timbers across the Thames to raise the Globe on Bankside. Hamlet, Othello, King Lear and Macbeth were written for that stage. In 1613 a cannon fired during a performance of Henry VIII set the thatch alight and the Globe burned to the ground.

Shakespeare invested his earnings in Stratford, where he had bought New Place in 1597, and died there in 1616. Seven years later his fellow actors John Heminges and Henry Condell published the First Folio, which preserved eighteen plays never printed before.
story.zh:
威廉·莎士比亚于1564年4月在埃文河畔斯特拉特福受洗，父亲是手套匠，也担任过镇上的公职。1582年他与安妮·海瑟薇结婚，育有三个孩子，此后有好几年文献中再无他的踪迹。到1592年，他已在伦敦小有名气：临终的作家罗伯特·格林讥讽有只“暴发户乌鸦”，自以为是全国唯一能“震撼舞台”的人。

从1594年起，他为宫内大臣剧团演戏和写作，詹姆斯一世即位后剧团改称国王剧团。剧团在肖迪奇的演出场所“剧场”租约到期后，他们在1598至1599年冬天把剧场拆掉，把木料运过泰晤士河，在南岸搭起了环球剧场。《哈姆雷特》《奥赛罗》《李尔王》和《麦克白》都是为这座舞台而写。1613年演出《亨利八世》时，一门礼炮点燃了屋顶的茅草，环球剧场被烧成平地。

莎士比亚把收入投资于故乡斯特拉特福，1597年在那里买下“新居”，1616年在那里去世。七年后，他的演员同伴约翰·赫明斯和亨利·康德尔出版了《第一对开本》，其中十八部剧作此前从未付印。

summary.en: The leading painter of the Dutch Golden Age, Rembrandt van Rijn moved from Leiden to Amsterdam in the early 1630s and became its most sought-after portraitist. His history paintings, etchings and searching self-portraits, including The Night Watch (1642), made him one of the most influential artists in Europe.
summary.zh: 伦勃朗·范赖恩是荷兰黄金时代最杰出的画家，17世纪30年代初从莱顿迁居阿姆斯特丹，成为当地最受追捧的肖像画家。他的历史画、蚀刻版画和深刻的自画像，以及《夜巡》（1642年）等作品，使他成为欧洲最具影响力的艺术家之一。

sources.title: Gary Schwartz, Rembrandt: His Life, His Paintings (1985)

story.en:
Born in Leiden, the son of a miller, Rembrandt briefly attended the university before choosing painting. Six months with the history painter Pieter Lastman in Amsterdam set his course, and by about 1631 he had moved there for good. Commissions poured in, and in 1634 he married Saskia van Uylenburgh, cousin of his art dealer.

The 1640s brought loss. Three of the couple's four children died in infancy, and Saskia died in 1642, the year he finished the vast militia group portrait now called The Night Watch. A popular story holds that the patrons rejected the picture and ruined him; historians find no evidence for that. It hung in the militia hall for decades and was trimmed in 1715 to fit a wall in the town hall.

His troubles were financial: he had bought an expensive house in 1639 and collected art beyond his means. In 1656 he sought a formal insolvency, and his possessions were auctioned. He kept working, producing some of his most profound late portraits, but outlived his companion Hendrickje Stoffels and his son Titus, and died in 1669.
story.zh:
伦勃朗出生于莱顿一个磨坊主家庭，曾短暂就读莱顿大学，后决意学画。他在阿姆斯特丹随历史画家彼得·拉斯特曼学习半年，从此确定了方向，约1631年移居阿姆斯特丹。订单接踵而至，1634年他娶了画商的表妹萨斯基亚·范·优伦堡。

17世纪40年代接连带来不幸：夫妇的四个孩子中有三个夭折，萨斯基亚也于1642年去世。同年他完成了为民兵连所作的巨幅群像，即今称《夜巡》的作品。流行的说法是委托人拒收此画、令他身败名裂，但史学家找不到任何证据。这幅画在民兵会所悬挂了数十年，1715年为挂进市政厅才被裁小。

他的困境其实源于财务：1639年他购入一座昂贵的宅邸，收藏艺术品也超出财力。1656年他申请破产清算，家产被拍卖。此后他仍坚持创作，留下许多最深沉的晚期肖像，却先后送走伴侣亨德里克耶·斯托弗尔斯和儿子提图斯，于1669年辞世。

summary.en: A Puritan gentleman farmer from Huntingdon, Cromwell rose through the English Civil Wars to command Parliament's armies, signed Charles I's death warrant and conquered Ireland and Scotland. From 1653 until his death he ruled England, Scotland and Ireland as Lord Protector.

sources.title: Antonia Fraser, Cromwell: Our Chief of Men (1973)

story.en:
Cromwell was a little-known MP and East Anglian landowner when civil war broke out in 1642. A religious conversion in the 1630s had convinced him that he was an instrument of Providence, and he raised a troop of disciplined, godly cavalry. At Marston Moor in 1644 and Naseby in 1645 his horsemen decided the battles, and he became the dominant figure in the New Model Army.

When Charles I kept intriguing after his defeat, Cromwell backed the purge of Parliament and the king's trial; he was the third of 59 commissioners to sign the death warrant, and Charles was beheaded at Whitehall in January 1649. Cromwell then invaded Ireland, where the killing of garrisons and civilians at Drogheda and Wexford is still bitterly remembered, and crushed the Scots at Dunbar and Worcester.

In 1653 he dissolved the Rump Parliament by force and became Lord Protector. He refused the crown in 1657 but ruled with near-regal power until his death in 1658. After the Restoration his body was exhumed and hanged at Tyburn, and his head was displayed at Westminster Hall.
story.zh:
1642年内战爆发时，克伦威尔还只是一名不太知名的议员和东英吉利地主。17世纪30年代的一次宗教皈依使他相信自己是天意的工具，他组建了一支纪律严明、信仰虔诚的骑兵。1644年的马斯顿荒原和1645年的内斯比，都是他的骑兵决定了胜负，他也因此成为新模范军中举足轻重的人物。

查理一世战败后仍暗中谋划，克伦威尔遂支持清洗议会、审判国王；在59名签署死刑令的法官中，他是第三个签名的。1649年1月，查理在白厅被斩首。随后克伦威尔进军爱尔兰，德罗赫达和韦克斯福德的守军与平民遭到屠杀，至今仍是爱尔兰人心中的伤痛；他又在邓巴和伍斯特击溃苏格兰军队。

1653年，他以武力解散残缺议会，就任护国公。1657年他拒绝了王冠，却以近乎君主的权力统治至1658年去世。王政复辟后，他的遗体被掘出，在泰伯恩刑场示众绞刑，首级则被悬挂在威斯敏斯特大厅。

summary.en: Louis XIV became king at four and reigned for 72 years, longer than any other European monarch. After Mazarin's death in 1661 he governed in person, moved the court to Versailles in 1682, fought repeated wars over France's frontiers and the Spanish succession, and revoked the Edict of Nantes in 1685.

sources.title: Peter Burke, The Fabrication of Louis XIV (1992)

story.en:
Louis was four when his father died in 1643, and his mother Anne of Austria governed with Cardinal Mazarin. The revolt of the Fronde marked him for life: in January 1649 the royal family slipped out of Paris by night to Saint-Germain, and the boy king learned to distrust both the capital and the great nobles.

When Mazarin died in 1661, Louis astonished his ministers by announcing that he would govern without a chief minister. With Colbert he reformed finances and built up industry and a navy; he patronised Molière, Racine and Lully; and he turned his father's hunting lodge at Versailles into a palace where the nobility competed for favour through elaborate ritual. The phrase 'L'État, c'est moi' is attributed to him, but there is no reliable evidence that he said it.

His wars won Franche-Comté and Strasbourg but raised ever larger coalitions against France, and the War of the Spanish Succession exhausted the treasury. The revocation of the Edict of Nantes drove perhaps 200,000 Huguenots abroad. He outlived his son and grandson and was succeeded by his five-year-old great-grandson, Louis XV.
story.zh:
1643年父王去世时路易年仅四岁，由母亲奥地利的安妮与红衣主教马萨林摄政。投石党运动给他留下终生烙印：1649年1月，王室连夜逃出巴黎前往圣日耳曼，少年国王从此对首都和大贵族都心怀戒备。

1661年马萨林去世，路易宣布不再设首席大臣、亲自主政，令大臣们大吃一惊。他与柯尔贝尔一道整顿财政，扶植工商业和海军；他资助莫里哀、拉辛和吕利；又把父亲在凡尔赛的狩猎行宫扩建为宏伟宫殿，让贵族们在繁复的礼仪中争宠。“朕即国家”这句话常被归于他名下，但并无可靠证据表明他说过。

他的战争为法国赢得了弗朗什-孔泰和斯特拉斯堡，却也招来越来越庞大的反法同盟，西班牙王位继承战争更使国库空虚。废除《南特敕令》迫使约二十万胡格诺派教徒流亡国外。他先后送走儿子和孙子，最终由年仅五岁的曾孙路易十五继位。

summary.en: Born François-Marie Arouet in Paris, Voltaire was imprisoned in the Bastille, exiled to England and lived for decades beyond easy reach of French censors. His plays, histories, Letters on the English and Candide made him the most famous writer of the Enlightenment and a relentless campaigner against religious intolerance.
summary.zh: 伏尔泰原名弗朗索瓦-马里·阿鲁埃，生于巴黎，曾被关进巴士底狱、流亡英国，此后数十年住在法国审查官鞭长莫及之处。他的戏剧、史著、《哲学通信》和《老实人》使他成为启蒙运动最负盛名的作家，也是反对宗教不宽容的不懈斗士。

sources.title: Roger Pearson, Voltaire Almighty: A Life in Pursuit of Freedom (2005)

story.en:
The son of a Paris notary, young Arouet was educated by the Jesuits and soon became known for his wit. Satirical verses cost him eleven months in the Bastille in 1717–18, after which he took the name Voltaire. In 1726 a quarrel with the Chevalier de Rohan, whose servants beat him, led to another spell in the Bastille and exile to England. There he admired religious toleration, Newton and Locke; his Letters on the English (1733–34) were burned in Paris as an attack on French institutions.

He spent most of the next fifteen years at Cirey with the mathematician Émilie du Châtelet, then joined Frederick the Great at Potsdam, a friendship that ended in a bitter falling-out in 1753. Settling near Geneva and then at Ferney, just inside France, he could cross a border if threatened.

From Ferney he published Candide (1759) and took up the case of Jean Calas, a Protestant executed in Toulouse in 1762, who was cleared in 1765. At 83 he returned to Paris; at a performance of his tragedy Irène his bust was crowned on stage. He died weeks later.
story.zh:
阿鲁埃是巴黎一位公证人之子，受耶稣会教育，很早便以机智闻名。1717至1718年，他因讽刺诗被关进巴士底狱十一个月，出狱后改名伏尔泰。1726年他与罗昂骑士发生争执，遭对方仆人殴打，随后再度入狱并被流放英国。他在英国钦佩那里的宗教宽容，推崇牛顿和洛克；《哲学通信》（1733至1734年）被视为攻击法国体制，在巴黎遭当众焚毁。

此后约十五年，他大多与数学家夏特莱侯爵夫人住在锡雷，后应腓特烈大帝之邀前往波茨坦，这段友谊于1753年不欢而散。他先定居日内瓦近郊，又迁到紧靠边界的法国小镇费尔内，一旦受威胁便可越境避险。

他在费尔内出版了《老实人》（1759年），并为1762年在图卢兹被处决的新教徒让·卡拉斯奔走申冤，卡拉斯终于在1765年获得平反。83岁时他重返巴黎，在其悲剧《伊雷娜》的演出中，人们在舞台上为他的胸像戴上桂冠。几周后，他与世长辞。

summary.en: A child prodigy from Salzburg who toured the courts of Europe with his father, Mozart settled in Vienna in 1781 as a freelance musician. In barely a decade there he wrote The Marriage of Figaro, Don Giovanni and The Magic Flute, along with concertos, symphonies and the unfinished Requiem.
summary.zh: 莫扎特是萨尔茨堡的神童，幼年随父亲巡游欧洲各国宫廷，1781年定居维也纳，成为自由音乐家。在此后短短十年里，他写下歌剧《费加罗的婚礼》《唐璜》《魔笛》，以及大量协奏曲、交响曲和未完成的《安魂曲》。

sources.title: Emily Anderson (ed.), The Letters of Mozart and His Family (3rd ed., 1985)

story.en:
Leopold Mozart, a violinist at the Salzburg court, recognised his son's gift early and took Wolfgang and his sister Nannerl on tour. Between 1763 and 1766 the family travelled through Germany to Paris and London, where the eight-year-old met Johann Christian Bach and composed his first symphonies. In Rome in 1770, Leopold reported, the boy heard Allegri's Miserere, a work the Sistine Chapel guarded jealously, and wrote it down from memory.

Back in Salzburg he chafed under Archbishop Colloredo, and in 1781 he left his service, by his own account with a kick from the archbishop's official Count Arco. In Vienna he married Constanze Weber, taught, gave subscription concerts and found in the librettist Lorenzo Da Ponte a partner for Figaro and Don Giovanni, the second a triumph in Prague.

Money ran short in the later 1780s, but his last year was productive: The Magic Flute opened in September 1791. He died on 5 December, aged 35, leaving the Requiem unfinished. The legend that his rival Salieri poisoned him has no basis.
story.zh:
萨尔茨堡宫廷小提琴手利奥波德·莫扎特很早就发现了儿子的天赋，带着沃尔夫冈和姐姐南内尔四处巡演。1763至1766年，一家人经德意志前往巴黎和伦敦；八岁的莫扎特在伦敦结识约翰·克里斯蒂安·巴赫，并写下最早的几部交响曲。据利奥波德的书信记载，1770年在罗马，少年莫扎特听了西斯廷礼拜堂秘不外传的阿莱格里《求主怜悯》，回去后便凭记忆把它完整写了出来。

回到萨尔茨堡后，他与科洛雷多大主教关系紧张，1781年脱离其宫廷；据他自己说，大主教的官员阿尔科伯爵还在他身后踹了一脚。在维也纳，他娶了康斯坦策·韦伯，靠教学和举办预约音乐会谋生，并与剧作家洛伦佐·达·蓬特合作了《费加罗的婚礼》和《唐璜》，后者在布拉格大获成功。

18世纪80年代后期他手头日益拮据，但最后一年依然多产，《魔笛》于1791年9月首演。同年12月5日，他在35岁时去世，《安魂曲》未能完成。所谓对手萨列里毒死他的传说毫无根据。

summary.en: A Scottish instrument maker, Watt realised in 1765 that a separate condenser would stop a steam engine wasting heat. In partnership with the Birmingham manufacturer Matthew Boulton from 1775 he built efficient pumping and rotary engines that powered mines, mills and factories; the unit of power bears his name.

label.en: Enters partnership with Matthew Boulton at Soho, Birmingham
label.zh: 在伯明翰索霍与马修·博尔顿合伙
卒于汉兹沃思的希思菲尔德府邸

sources.title: Richard L. Hills, James Watt (3 vols, 2002–2006)

story.en:
Watt grew up in the port of Greenock and trained as a mathematical-instrument maker in London before the University of Glasgow gave him a workshop in 1757. In 1763–64 he was asked to repair the university's model of a Newcomen engine and saw how much steam it wasted: the cylinder had to be heated and cooled again on every stroke.

Watt later recalled that the answer came to him on a Sunday walk across Glasgow Green in May 1765: condense the steam in a separate vessel, so the cylinder could stay hot. The familiar tale of the boy watching a kettle rests on later family reminiscence. Turning the idea into a working engine took a decade. His first backer, John Roebuck, went bankrupt, and Watt worked as a canal surveyor to support his family.

In 1774 he moved to Birmingham, where Matthew Boulton took over Roebuck's share, and Parliament extended the patent to 1800. Boulton & Watt engines, which used roughly a quarter of the fuel of the old design, spread from Cornish mines to cotton mills once Watt added rotary motion. A member of the Lunar Society, he retired wealthy and died at Heathfield in 1819.
story.zh:
瓦特在港口小城格里诺克长大，曾在伦敦学习数学仪器制作，1757年格拉斯哥大学为他提供了一间作坊。1763至1764年，他受托修理大学的纽科门蒸汽机模型，发现它浪费了大量蒸汽：每一个冲程，汽缸都要重新加热、再次冷却。

据瓦特晚年回忆，1765年5月一个星期日，他在格拉斯哥绿地散步时想到了办法：让蒸汽在另一个容器中冷凝，汽缸便可一直保持高温。至于他幼年盯着水壶出神的故事，不过出自后来的家族回忆。把构想变成可用的机器花了整整十年：他的第一位资助人约翰·罗巴克破产，瓦特只得靠勘测运河养家。

1774年他迁居伯明翰，马修·博尔顿接手了罗巴克的股份，议会又把专利延长到1800年。博尔顿-瓦特蒸汽机的耗煤量只有旧式机器的四分之一左右，在瓦特加上旋转运动装置后，从康沃尔的矿山推广到各地棉纺厂。他是月光社成员，晚年富足退休，1819年在希思菲尔德去世。

summary.en: A largely self-taught London writer, Mary Wollstonecraft argued in A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792) that women seem inferior only because they are denied education. She witnessed the French Revolution in Paris, travelled in Scandinavia, and died soon after giving birth to the future Mary Shelley.
summary.zh: 玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特是一位基本靠自学成才的伦敦作家，她在《女权辩护》（1792年）中指出，女性显得低人一等，只是因为她们被剥夺了受教育的机会。她曾在巴黎亲历法国大革命，又游历斯堪的纳维亚，生下日后的玛丽·雪莱后不久便去世。

label.zh: 生于伦敦斯皮塔佛德

label.en: Opens a school at Newington Green
label.zh: 在纽因顿格林开办学校

label.en: Nurses her friend Fanny Blood in Lisbon
label.zh: 赴里斯本照料好友范妮·布拉德

label.zh: 在米切尔斯敦为金斯伯勒家族当家庭教师

label.zh: 出版《女权辩护》

label.zh: 游历斯堪的纳维亚，暂居滕斯贝格

label.zh: 卒于萨默斯镇波利冈

sources.title: Claire Tomalin, The Life and Death of Mary Wollstonecraft (1974)
Janet Todd, Mary Wollstonecraft: A Revolutionary Life (2000)

story.en:
Mary Wollstonecraft grew up in a household run down by her father's drinking and failed farming ventures. With her sisters and her close friend Fanny Blood she opened a school at Newington Green, where she met the Dissenting minister Richard Price. After Fanny died in childbirth in Lisbon, and a year as a governess in Ireland, she went to London determined to live by her pen, backed by the radical publisher Joseph Johnson.

When Edmund Burke attacked the French Revolution, she answered within weeks with A Vindication of the Rights of Men (1790), and followed it with A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, which argued that reason and virtue have no sex. In Paris during the Terror she fell in love with the American Gilbert Imlay and bore a daughter, Fanny. His desertion drove her to two suicide attempts, one by leaping from Putney Bridge, yet the letters she wrote on a business trip to Scandinavia for him became a much-admired travel book.

In 1797 she married the philosopher William Godwin. Eleven days after giving birth to their daughter Mary, she died of puerperal fever.
story.zh:
玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特的父亲酗酒、务农屡屡失败，家道因此中落。她与姐妹们以及挚友范妮·布拉德在纽因顿格林开办学校，在那里结识了非国教派牧师理查德·普赖斯。范妮在里斯本死于难产，她又在爱尔兰当了一年家庭教师，之后来到伦敦，在激进派出版商约瑟夫·约翰逊的支持下决心以写作为生。

埃德蒙·伯克抨击法国大革命后，她在数周内便写出《人权辩护》（1790年）予以回击，随后又发表《女权辩护》，主张理性和美德并无性别之分。恐怖统治时期她身在巴黎，与美国人吉尔伯特·伊姆利相恋，生下女儿范妮。伊姆利的背弃使她两度自杀，其中一次是从普特尼桥纵身跳入泰晤士河；然而她替伊姆利赴斯堪的纳维亚处理生意时写下的书信，却成了广受赞誉的游记。

1797年，她与哲学家威廉·葛德文结婚。生下女儿玛丽十一天后，她因产褥热去世。

summary.en: After five years as naturalist on HMS Beagle, Charles Darwin spent two decades at Down House assembling evidence for evolution by natural selection, an idea Alfred Russel Wallace reached independently. On the Origin of Species (1859) transformed biology and remains the foundation of the life sciences.
summary.zh: 查尔斯·达尔文随“小猎犬”号航行五年后，在唐恩宅邸花了二十年搜集证据，论证以自然选择为机制的进化论，阿尔弗雷德·拉塞尔·华莱士也独立得出了同样的思想。《物种起源》（1859年）彻底改变了生物学，至今仍是生命科学的基础。

在爱丁堡学医
就读剑桥基督学院

label.zh: 乘“小猎犬”号从普利茅斯启航
考察加拉帕戈斯群岛
定居肯特郡唐恩宅邸

label.en: Joint Darwin–Wallace papers read at the Linnean Society
label.zh: 达尔文与华莱士的论文在林奈学会一并宣读

label.en: Dies at Down House; buried in Westminster Abbey
label.zh: 卒于唐恩宅邸，葬于威斯敏斯特教堂

sources.title: Janet Browne, Charles Darwin: Voyaging (1995) and The Power of Place (2002)
Darwin Correspondence Project, University of Cambridge

story.en:
Darwin abandoned medicine at Edinburgh and was preparing for the Church at Cambridge when the botanist John Henslow recommended him as gentleman companion and naturalist for Captain Robert FitzRoy's survey ship Beagle. The voyage of 1831–36 took him round South America, where he dug up fossils of giant extinct mammals, and in September 1835 to the Galápagos. He noticed that the mockingbirds differed from island to island; the famous finches became significant only later, when the ornithologist John Gould examined them in London.

By 1838, after reading Malthus on population, Darwin had the idea of natural selection, but he spent twenty years quietly gathering evidence at Down House while suffering chronic illness. In June 1858 a letter from Alfred Russel Wallace in the Malay Archipelago outlined the same theory, and friends arranged for both men's papers to be read together at the Linnean Society.

On the Origin of Species appeared in November 1859, and the first printing was taken up by booksellers at once. It provoked fierce debate but persuaded most scientists of evolution within two decades. Darwin was buried in Westminster Abbey in 1882.
story.zh:
达尔文在爱丁堡放弃学医，后在剑桥准备担任神职。这时植物学家约翰·亨斯洛推荐他担任罗伯特·菲茨罗伊舰长的测量船“小猎犬”号上的随船绅士兼博物学家。1831至1836年的航行带他环绕南美洲，他在那里发掘了已灭绝巨型哺乳动物的化石，并于1835年9月抵达加拉帕戈斯群岛。他注意到各岛的嘲鸫互不相同；那些著名的雀鸟则是后来经鸟类学家约翰·古尔德在伦敦鉴定，才显出其意义。

到1838年，达尔文在阅读马尔萨斯的人口论后形成了自然选择的构想，但此后二十年，他一边忍受慢性病折磨，一边在唐恩宅邸默默积累证据。1858年6月，身在马来群岛的阿尔弗雷德·拉塞尔·华莱士来信，阐述了同样的理论，朋友们于是安排两人的论文在林奈学会一并宣读。

《物种起源》于1859年11月出版，首印随即被书商订购一空。它引发了激烈争论，但不到二十年便使大多数科学家接受了进化论。1882年，达尔文安葬于威斯敏斯特教堂。

role.zh: 意大利复兴运动革命将领

summary.en: Born in Nice, Garibaldi spent his years of exile fighting in South American wars before returning to defend the Roman Republic in 1849. In 1860 his volunteer Thousand conquered Sicily and Naples, which he handed to Victor Emmanuel II, opening the way to the Kingdom of Italy.
summary.zh: 加里波第生于尼斯，流亡期间投身南美洲的战争，1849年回国保卫罗马共和国。1860年，他率领“千人团”志愿军征服西西里和那不勒斯，并将其交给维克托·伊曼纽尔二世，为意大利王国的建立铺平了道路。

label.zh: 生于尼斯

label.zh: 在塔甘罗格接受马志尼的主张

label.zh: 在蒙得维的亚率领意大利军团

label.zh: 在贾尼科洛山保卫罗马共和国

label.zh: 率“千人团”在马尔萨拉登陆

label.en: Hands his conquests to Victor Emmanuel II near Teano
label.zh: 在泰阿诺附近把征服的土地交给维克托·伊曼纽尔二世
卒于卡普雷拉岛

sources.title: Lucy Riall, Garibaldi: Invention of a Hero (2007)
Denis Mack Smith, Garibaldi: A Great Life in Brief (1956)

story.en:
A merchant sailor from Nice, Garibaldi joined Giuseppe Mazzini's Young Italy after a chance meeting with one of its members in the Black Sea port of Taganrog. A failed rising in 1834 brought a death sentence in absentia, and he fled to South America. For twelve years he fought for the rebel republic of Rio Grande do Sul and then for Montevideo, where his Italian Legion adopted the red shirts later famous in Italy, and he met Anita Ribeiro da Silva, who rode with him into battle.

Back in Italy in 1848, he led the defence of the Roman Republic against the French in 1849. During the retreat Anita, pregnant and ill, died near Ravenna.

His great stroke came in May 1860, when he sailed from near Genoa with about a thousand volunteers, landed at Marsala and, joined by Sicilian rebels, took Palermo and then Naples. Near Teano in October he greeted Victor Emmanuel II as king of Italy and withdrew to his island farm on Caprera. Later attempts to seize Rome failed, but he remained Italy's most popular hero.
story.zh:
加里波第是尼斯的商船水手，一次在黑海港口塔甘罗格偶遇“青年意大利”成员，从此加入朱塞佩·马志尼的组织。1834年起义失败后，他被缺席判处死刑，逃往南美洲。此后十二年间，他先为南里奥格兰德的反叛共和国作战，后来保卫蒙得维的亚；他的意大利军团在那里穿上了日后闻名意大利的红衫，他也结识了与他并肩上阵的安妮塔·里贝罗·达·席尔瓦。

1848年他回到意大利，次年领导罗马共和国抵抗法军。撤退途中，怀有身孕又身患重病的安妮塔死于拉文纳附近。

他最辉煌的一击发生在1860年5月：他带领约一千名志愿者从热那亚附近出海，在马尔萨拉登陆，在西西里起义者的响应下攻占巴勒莫，又进占那不勒斯。10月，他在泰阿诺附近向维克托·伊曼纽尔二世致意，尊其为意大利国王，随后退隐卡普雷拉岛上的农庄。他此后几次试图夺取罗马均告失败，却始终是意大利最受爱戴的英雄。

role.zh: 普鲁士首相、德意志帝国宰相

summary.en: A Junker from Brandenburg, Bismarck became Prussia's minister-president in 1862 and, through wars with Denmark, Austria and France, united Germany under the Prussian crown in 1871. As imperial chancellor until 1890 he built a defensive alliance system and introduced the first national social insurance.
summary.zh: 俾斯麦是勃兰登堡的容克贵族，1862年出任普鲁士首相，通过对丹麦、奥地利和法国的三场战争，于1871年在普鲁士王室之下统一德国。他担任帝国宰相至1890年，构建了防御性同盟体系，并推行了世界上最早的全国性社会保险。

label.zh: 生于舍恩豪森
在哥廷根学习法律

label.zh: 在柏林出任普鲁士首相

label.zh: 随国王威廉亲临克尼格雷茨战场
德意志帝国在凡尔赛宣告成立
卒于弗里德里希斯鲁

sources.title: Otto Pflanze, Bismarck and the Development of Germany (3 vols, 1990)

story.en:
Bismarck was a hard-drinking country squire who made his name in 1847 as an ultra-conservative deputy in the Prussian United Diet. Diplomatic posts in Frankfurt, St Petersburg and Paris taught him the balance of European power. In 1862, when King William I was deadlocked with the liberals over army reform, he made Bismarck minister-president. A week later Bismarck told a budget committee that the great questions of the day would be decided not by speeches and majority resolutions but by iron and blood.

He then fought three short wars: with Austria against Denmark in 1864, against Austria in 1866, decided at Königgrätz, and against France in 1870–71, a war he helped provoke by editing the Ems telegram. On 18 January 1871 William was proclaimed German emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.

As chancellor, Bismarck sought peace through alliances and hosted the Congress of Berlin in 1878. At home he fought the Catholic Church and the socialists, and created health, accident and old-age insurance. The young William II dismissed him in 1890, and he died at Friedrichsruh eight years later.
story.zh:
俾斯麦原是一位嗜酒的乡村地主，1847年作为极端保守派议员在普鲁士联合议会中崭露头角。在法兰克福、圣彼得堡和巴黎的外交任职，让他深谙欧洲列强的均势之道。1862年，国王威廉一世因军队改革与自由派僵持不下，任命俾斯麦为首相。一周后，俾斯麦在预算委员会上宣称，当代的重大问题不是靠演说和多数决议，而是要靠铁和血来解决。

随后他发动了三场短暂的战争：1864年联合奥地利对丹麦作战；1866年对奥地利开战，在克尼格雷茨一役定胜负；1870至1871年对法国作战，而这场战争部分正是由他删改“埃姆斯密电”挑起的。1871年1月18日，威廉在凡尔赛宫镜厅被拥立为德意志皇帝。

担任宰相期间，俾斯麦力图以同盟体系维持和平，1878年主持柏林会议；对内则打压天主教会和社会主义者，并建立了疾病、工伤和养老保险制度。1890年，年轻的威廉二世将他免职，八年后他在弗里德里希斯鲁去世。

role.zh: 哲学家、经济学家、革命家

summary.en: Born in Trier, Karl Marx was a radical journalist expelled from France, Belgium and Prussia before settling in London in 1849. With Friedrich Engels he wrote The Communist Manifesto (1848); his Capital (1867) analysed capitalism and became the founding text of movements that reshaped the twentieth century.
summary.zh: 卡尔·马克思生于特里尔，作为激进记者先后被法国、比利时和普鲁士驱逐，1849年定居伦敦。他与弗里德里希·恩格斯合著《共产党宣言》（1848年）；他的《资本论》（1867年）剖析了资本主义，成为深刻改变二十世纪的诸多运动的奠基之作。

sources.title: Gareth Stedman Jones, Karl Marx: Greatness and Illusion (2016)
Jonathan Sperber, Karl Marx: A Nineteenth-Century Life (2013)

story.en:
The son of a lawyer who had converted from Judaism, Marx studied law and then philosophy in Berlin among the Young Hegelians. Barred from an academic career, he edited the liberal Rheinische Zeitung in Cologne until the Prussian authorities suppressed it in 1843. In Paris he met Friedrich Engels, the son of a textile manufacturer, and began a lifelong partnership.

Expelled from France, Marx moved to Brussels, where the two men wrote The Communist Manifesto for a small workers' league; it appeared in London in February 1848, just as revolution swept Europe. After the revolutions failed, Marx settled in London. For years the family lived in poverty in two rooms in Soho, where three of their children died, while Engels sent money from Manchester and Marx worked in the British Museum reading room.

The first volume of Capital was published in Hamburg in 1867; Engels edited the later volumes after Marx's death. From 1864 Marx helped lead the International Working Men's Association. He died in his armchair in March 1883, fifteen months after his wife Jenny, and was buried at Highgate Cemetery.
story.zh:
马克思的父亲是一位已从犹太教改宗的律师。马克思先学法律，后在柏林的青年黑格尔派圈子中研习哲学。他无法走上学术道路，便在科隆主编自由派的《莱茵报》，直到1843年该报被普鲁士当局查封。在巴黎，他结识了纺织厂主之子弗里德里希·恩格斯，两人从此结下终身的合作关系。

被法国驱逐后，马克思迁往布鲁塞尔，与恩格斯一起为一个小小的工人同盟起草了《共产党宣言》；1848年2月，它在伦敦出版，恰逢革命席卷欧洲。革命失败后，马克思定居伦敦。一家人多年挤在苏豪区的两间屋子里，过着贫困的生活，三个孩子在那里夭折；恩格斯从曼彻斯特寄钱接济，马克思则在大英博物馆阅览室埋头研究。

《资本论》第一卷于1867年在汉堡出版，其余各卷由恩格斯在他身后整理出版。1864年起，马克思参与领导国际工人协会。1883年3月，在妻子燕妮去世十五个月后，他在扶手椅上溘然长逝，葬于海格特公墓。

role.en: Founder of modern nursing and statistician
role.zh: 现代护理学奠基人、统计学家

summary.en: Named after the city of her birth, Florence Nightingale defied her wealthy family to train as a nurse and in 1854 led a party of nurses to the British army hospital at Scutari in the Crimean War. Her statistical campaigns for sanitary reform and her school at St Thomas' Hospital made nursing a profession.
summary.zh: 弗洛伦丝·南丁格尔以出生地佛罗伦萨命名，她不顾富裕家庭的反对立志学习护理，1854年克里米亚战争期间率领护士队前往斯库塔里的英国陆军医院。她以统计数据推动卫生改革，又在圣托马斯医院创办护士学校，使护理成为一门专业。

label.zh: 在恩布利庄园感到“神召”

sources.title: Mark Bostridge, Florence Nightingale: The Woman and Her Legend (2008)
Lynn McDonald (ed.), The Collected Works of Florence Nightingale (2001–2012)

story.en:
Florence Nightingale was born in 1820 during her wealthy parents' long tour of Italy. At sixteen, at Embley, she felt that God had called her to his service, but her family opposed her wish to nurse, then a disreputable occupation. Only in 1851 did she manage to train at the Protestant deaconess institute at Kaiserswerth on the Rhine.

In 1854, after reports in The Times on the suffering of wounded soldiers in the Crimean War, her friend Sidney Herbert, the Secretary at War, sent her with 38 nurses to the army hospital at Scutari, across the Bosporus from Constantinople. She organised supplies, laundry and food in a filthy, overcrowded building; her night rounds inspired the image of the 'Lady with the Lamp'. Deaths fell sharply only after a sanitary commission cleared drains and improved ventilation in spring 1855, a lesson she took to heart.

Back in England she used statistics and her polar-area diagrams to press for army health reform, became the first woman elected to the Statistical Society of London, and founded her nursing school in 1860. Though often bedridden, she worked into old age and died in 1910.
story.zh:
1820年，南丁格尔的富裕父母在意大利长途游历时生下了她。十六岁那年，她在恩布利庄园感到上帝召唤她献身服务，但家人坚决反对她当护士——那在当时被视为不体面的职业。直到1851年，她才得以前往莱茵河畔凯泽斯韦特的新教女执事院接受训练。

1854年，《泰晤士报》报道了克里米亚战争中伤兵的惨状，她的朋友、陆军大臣西德尼·赫伯特随即派她带领38名护士前往斯库塔里的陆军医院，那里与君士坦丁堡隔博斯普鲁斯海峡相望。在那座肮脏拥挤的建筑里，她整顿物资、洗衣和伙食；她深夜提灯查房的身影，造就了“提灯女士”的形象。直到1855年春卫生委员会疏通排水、改善通风后，死亡率才大幅下降，她从中深刻汲取了教训。

回到英国后，她用统计数据和极区图推动军队卫生改革，成为首位当选伦敦统计学会会员的女性，并于1860年创办护士学校。尽管长年卧床，她一直工作到晚年，1910年辞世。

summary.en: A Manchester radical, Emmeline Pankhurst founded the Women's Social and Political Union in 1903 and led its militant campaign for votes for women, enduring repeated imprisonment and hunger strikes. She suspended militancy in 1914 to support the war effort; British women won the vote on equal terms with men weeks after her death in 1928.

sources.title: June Purvis, Emmeline Pankhurst: A Biography (2002)

story.en:
Emmeline Goulden grew up in a radical Manchester household and, by her own account, attended her first women's suffrage meeting at fourteen. In 1879 she married Richard Pankhurst, a barrister who had drafted early women's suffrage bills. After his death in 1898, frustrated by decades of polite petitioning, she founded the Women's Social and Political Union at her Manchester home in 1903, with her daughter Christabel soon its chief strategist. Its motto was 'Deeds, not words'.

The Daily Mail coined the word 'suffragettes' as a sneer; the WSPU adopted it with pride. After 1908 peaceful mass rallies gave way to window-smashing, arson and bombs. Imprisoned suffragettes went on hunger strike and were force-fed; the 1913 'Cat and Mouse Act' let the government release and rearrest them, and Pankhurst herself was jailed again and again.

When war came in 1914 she halted militancy and campaigned for recruitment and women's war work. In 1918 women over thirty won the vote. Pankhurst died on 14 June 1928, shortly before the act giving women the vote on the same terms as men became law.
story.zh:
埃米琳·古尔登在曼彻斯特一个激进派家庭长大，据她自述，十四岁时第一次参加争取妇女选举权的集会。1879年，她嫁给律师理查德·潘克斯特，他曾起草早期的妇女选举权法案。1898年丈夫去世后，她对几十年温和请愿毫无成效深感失望，于1903年在曼彻斯特家中创立妇女社会政治联盟，女儿克丽斯特布尔很快成为联盟的主要策划者。联盟的口号是“要行动，不要空谈”。

“suffragette”（女参政者）一词原是《每日邮报》的讥讽之语，联盟却骄傲地接过了这个称号。1908年以后，和平的群众集会逐渐让位于砸窗、纵火和炸弹。入狱的成员绝食抗议，遭到强制灌食；1913年的“猫捉老鼠法”允许政府先释放绝食者、待其康复后再行逮捕，潘克斯特本人也一再入狱。

1914年战争爆发，她停止激进行动，转而为征兵和妇女参加战时工作奔走。1918年，三十岁以上的妇女获得选举权。1928年6月14日潘克斯特去世，不久之后，赋予妇女与男子同等选举权的法案便正式成为法律。

summary.en: Born in Ulm, Albert Einstein published his papers on light quanta, Brownian motion and special relativity in 1905 while working at the Swiss patent office, and completed general relativity in Berlin in 1915. He received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics and emigrated to Princeton after the Nazis came to power.

sources.title: Walter Isaacson, Einstein: His Life and Universe (2007)
Abraham Pais, 'Subtle Is the Lord': The Science and the Life of Albert Einstein (1982)

story.en:
Einstein was a gifted but rebellious pupil who left his Munich school without finishing, trained as a physics teacher at the Zurich Polytechnic and, unable to find a university post, took a job at the patent office in Bern in 1902. In 1905, working there in his spare time, he published papers explaining the photoelectric effect with light quanta, showing how Brownian motion revealed the reality of atoms, and setting out special relativity, with its corollary E = mc².

Professorships in Zurich and Prague followed, and in 1914 a research post in Berlin, where he completed the general theory of relativity in November 1915. In 1919 British expeditions organised by Arthur Eddington found that starlight was bent by the Sun during an eclipse, as he had predicted, and he became world-famous almost overnight. His Nobel Prize for 1921, awarded in 1922, cited the photoelectric effect rather than relativity.

As a Jew, a pacifist and a celebrity, he was a target for the Nazis. He was abroad when they took power in 1933 and never returned. At Princeton he sought a unified field theory, and in 1939 he signed a letter urging President Roosevelt to support atomic research.
story.zh:
爱因斯坦天资出众却桀骜不驯，未读完慕尼黑的中学便离校，后在苏黎世联邦理工学院接受物理教师培训。他找不到大学教职，1902年进入伯尔尼专利局工作。1905年，他利用业余时间发表了一系列论文：用光量子解释光电效应，说明布朗运动如何揭示原子的真实存在，并提出狭义相对论及其推论E = mc²。

此后他先后在苏黎世和布拉格任教授，1914年赴柏林担任研究职位，并于1915年11月完成广义相对论。1919年，由亚瑟·爱丁顿组织的英国观测队在日食期间测得星光经过太阳时发生偏折，与他的预言相符，他几乎一夜之间名扬世界。他获颁的1921年度诺贝尔物理学奖（1922年颁发）表彰的是光电效应，而非相对论。

身为犹太人、和平主义者和名人，他成了纳粹的攻击目标。1933年纳粹上台时他正在国外，从此再未回国。他在普林斯顿致力于探索统一场论；1939年，他签署了一封信，敦促罗斯福总统支持原子能研究。

summary.en: An Austrian-born failed artist and First World War veteran, Hitler led the Nazi Party to power in Germany in 1933 and made himself dictator. His regime started the Second World War in Europe and carried out the Holocaust, the murder of about six million Jews. He killed himself in Berlin in April 1945.

Ian Kershaw, Hitler: 1889–1936 Hubris (1998) and 1936–1945 Nemesis (2000)

story.en:
Hitler drifted through Vienna as a would-be artist after the Academy of Fine Arts rejected him twice, absorbing the city's antisemitic and pan-German politics. In 1914 he volunteered for the Bavarian army, served as a regimental runner and was decorated. Germany's defeat, which he blamed on Jews and Marxists, turned him to politics, and in Munich he became leader of the small Nazi Party.

His Beer Hall Putsch of November 1923 failed, and in Landsberg prison he dictated Mein Kampf. During the Depression the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag, and on 30 January 1933 President Hindenburg appointed him chancellor. Within months he had abolished rival parties, free trade unions and a free press; in 1934 he made himself Führer.

His drive for conquest led to the invasion of Poland in September 1939. After the attack on the Soviet Union in 1941 his regime moved to the systematic murder of Europe's Jews: about six million were killed in mass shootings and in camps such as Auschwitz, along with millions of other victims. As Soviet troops fought their way into Berlin, he shot himself in his bunker on 30 April 1945.
story.zh:
希特勒两度报考维也纳美术学院均落榜，此后以落魄画家的身份在维也纳游荡，耳濡目染了当地的反犹主义和泛日耳曼主义政治。1914年他自愿加入巴伐利亚军队，担任团部传令兵并获得勋章。他把德国战败归咎于犹太人和马克思主义者，由此投身政治，在慕尼黑成为弱小的纳粹党的领袖。

1923年11月，他发动的啤酒馆政变失败，在兰茨贝格监狱中口述了《我的奋斗》。大萧条期间纳粹党跃升为国会第一大党，1933年1月30日，兴登堡总统任命他为总理。短短数月间，他取缔了其他政党、自由工会和新闻自由；1934年，他自封为“元首”。

他的扩张野心导致1939年9月入侵波兰。1941年进攻苏联后，纳粹政权开始有计划地屠杀欧洲犹太人：约六百万犹太人在大规模枪决和奥斯维辛等集中营中遇害，另有数以百万计的其他受害者。苏军攻入柏林之际，他于1945年4月30日在地堡中开枪自尽。

He headed the provisional government after the liberation, returned to power in 1958 to found the Fifth Republic, and as president ended the Algerian War.

sources.title: Julian Jackson, A Certain Idea of France: The Life of Charles de Gaulle (2018)

story.en:
De Gaulle was a young captain at Verdun in 1916 when he was bayoneted and taken prisoner; five escape attempts failed. Between the wars he argued, largely in vain, for mobile armoured forces. In May 1940 he commanded a tank division and in June briefly joined the government as an under-secretary for war. When Marshal Pétain sought an armistice, he flew to London and on 18 June declared on the BBC that the flame of French resistance must not go out. Few heard the broadcast at the time, and Vichy sentenced him to death in absentia.

From London, Brazzaville and later Algiers he built Free France into a government-in-waiting, often clashing with Churchill and Roosevelt. On 26 August 1944 he walked down the Champs-Élysées before vast crowds.

He resigned in 1946, but the Algerian crisis brought him back in 1958. The Fifth Republic's constitution gave the president strong powers; he accepted Algerian independence in 1962, built a French nuclear force and withdrew from NATO's integrated command. After the upheaval of May 1968 and a lost referendum in 1969 he retired to Colombey, where he died in 1970.
story.zh:
1916年在凡尔登，年轻的上尉戴高乐被刺刀刺伤后被俘，他五次越狱均未成功。两次大战之间，他力主建立机动装甲部队，却鲜有人采纳。1940年5月他指挥一个装甲师，6月短暂入阁，出任负责国防和陆军事务的副国务秘书。贝当元帅寻求停战时，他飞往伦敦，6月18日通过BBC广播宣称，法国抵抗的火焰绝不能熄灭。当时听到这篇讲话的人寥寥无几，维希政府则缺席判处他死刑。

他先后以伦敦、布拉柴维尔和阿尔及尔为基地，把自由法国打造成一个蓄势待发的流亡政府，与丘吉尔和罗斯福屡有冲突。1944年8月26日，他在人山人海中沿香榭丽舍大街步行而下。

1946年他辞职下野，阿尔及利亚危机又使他于1958年东山再起。第五共和国宪法赋予总统强大权力；他于1962年接受阿尔及利亚独立，建立法国独立核力量，并退出北约军事一体化指挥机构。经历1968年五月风暴和1969年公投失利后，他退居科隆贝，1970年在那里去世。

summary.en: A German-Jewish girl whose family fled to Amsterdam in 1933–34, Anne Frank hid with seven others in a secret annex behind her father's business from 1942 to 1944. After their arrest she was deported and died at Bergen-Belsen in early 1945. Her diary became one of the most widely read books about the Holocaust.

note: Exact date of death unknown. The Dutch authorities long gave 31 March 1945; Anne Frank House research (2015) concludes she probably died in February 1945.

story.en:
Anne Frank was four when her father, Otto, moved his business to Amsterdam after the Nazis came to power, and the family followed him. The German invasion of the Netherlands in 1940 brought them back under Nazi rule. In July 1942, after Anne's sister Margot received a call-up for a 'labour camp', the family hid in rooms behind Otto's firm on the Prinsengracht, later joined by four others. Helpers from his staff, among them Miep Gies, brought food and news.

Anne had received a diary for her thirteenth birthday, and in hiding she wrote with growing skill, revising entries after a 1944 radio appeal to keep wartime records. On 4 August 1944 the police raided the annex; whether anyone betrayed them, and who, remains unknown.

The eight were sent via Westerbork to Auschwitz on the last transport from that camp. In late October Anne and Margot were moved to Bergen-Belsen, where both died of typhus in the winter of 1945, probably in February. Otto, the only one of the eight to survive, received the diary papers Miep had saved and published them in 1947.
story.zh:
纳粹上台后，安妮的父亲奥托把生意迁到阿姆斯特丹，一家人随后迁居，当时安妮四岁。1940年德国入侵荷兰，他们再次落入纳粹统治之下。1942年7月，安妮的姐姐玛戈特接到前往“劳动营”的征召令，全家随即躲进王子运河畔奥托公司后部的房间，后来又有四人加入。米普·希斯等公司员工冒险为他们送来食物和消息。

安妮在十三岁生日时得到一本日记。藏匿期间，她的文笔日益成熟；1944年听到电台呼吁人们保存战时记录后，她还着手修改日记。1944年8月4日，警察突袭了密室；究竟有没有人告密、告密者又是谁，至今仍无定论。

八人经韦斯特博克中转营，搭乘该营开往奥斯维辛的最后一班列车被押走。10月下旬，安妮和玛戈特被转到贝尔根-贝尔森，1945年冬两人相继死于斑疹伤寒，时间很可能在2月。八人中唯一幸存的奥托从米普手中接过她保存下来的日记手稿，于1947年将其出版。
